title: Matthias (Acts 1:12–26)
hookLine: they pray, with the women and Mary, and choose a replacement for Judas
tomorrow: a room of Galileans speaks, and every visitor hears…

cards: Before a choir sings a single song, it often finds one note together, everyone humming until the room buzzes as one sound. Acts 1 starts a hard choice that way. Twelve have become eleven, and a place is empty.

Before anyone names a candidate, they go up into an upper room, and Acts lists who's there: "These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren."
One sound first. Then the choice.

teach.h: SOMEONE WHO WAS THERE THE WHOLE WAY.
teach.b: Peter's test for the new person is plain: someone who was with them the whole way, from John's baptism to the day Jesus was taken up, "to be a witness with us of his resurrection."
Witness: yesterday's word, straight back. Two names fit: "Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias."
Then, before anything is settled, they pray: "Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen." And they cast lots, something like drawing straws.
"And the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles." Notice what the text does with both men. Matthias makes no speech; in this chapter he never says a word.
Joseph Barsabas isn't chosen, and Acts never says how he took it. Both were there the whole way. One gets the place.
So the prayer isn't a request for a good outcome. It's an admission: you know the hearts, and we don't.
One to tell a friend tonight: with one accord is a single Greek word, homothumadon, with one mind.
It describes the room before it describes the choice. They got quiet together, and only then did they choose.

how: Some churches keep a feast day for Saint Matthias and read Acts 1:15–26 on it; some congregations pray together before choosing leaders.

games.why: they did cast lots, but only after they all continued with one accord in prayer and asked the one who knows the hearts.

practice: Let your breath out on a low, easy hum, and feel where it buzzes: lips, throat, chest. Keep humming one steady note on each out-breath.
If a choice is waiting for you, let it sit inside that one sound without picking yet, the way the room prayed before it chose.

wordCard.voice: Matthias. The one chosen to fill the empty place, after prayer and by lot, who never says a word in the story.

orig.note: Greek: with one accord, with one mind. Acts 1:14, the room praying together before the choice.

carryVoice: Keep this: with one accord, the quiet together first and the choosing after. Day two of Acts.
